A1.justification: Both 30-page PDFs describe PreferThinker and contain complete main text and Appendices A–F. Text and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, figures and appendix material despite image recompression.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and ablation results in Tables 1–3, robustness experiments in Figure 7, and a 100-participant preference-element study in Appendix B.1 and Figure S1.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark, ablation, robustness and user-study results, including Tables 1–3, Figure 7 and Figure S1.

M1.justification: The predict-then-assess procedure, Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbone, cold-start SFT, GRPO training and similarity-aware prediction reward remain unchanged in Section 3.

E1.justification: PreferImg/PreferImg-CoT, user-grouped PickaPic, and the appendix single-image scoring and personalized-generation examples are retained. No dataset, population or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparison methods, including PickScore, ViPer, UnifiedReward and UnifiedReward-Think. Table 3 and Figure 7 also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same 1,500-sample PreferImg benchmark, 894 PickaPic samples, preference categories, seen/unseen partitions, metrics and experimental settings.

E4.justification: The SFT/RL/prediction-reward ablations, reference-count robustness tests, and appendix reasoning, transferability, generation and failure-case analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, Figure 7 and the appendix examples retain the same results. For example, Table 1 reports PreferThinker’s average accuracy as 88.7 and PickaPic accuracy as 65.7 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including the training objectives and similarity/reward definitions, are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about preference profiles, interpretable assessment, the CoT dataset, training strategy and prediction reward.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged. Appendix E.4 retains the limitations concerning synthetic profiles, five visual attributes and complex real-user preferences.

D1.justification: Implementation frameworks, hyperparameters, hardware and training times in Appendix A, prompt templates in Appendix C, and the project-page link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to general preference assessment, ViPer and reasoning-based reward models.

P1.justification: The correspondence symbol moves from Wangmeng Zuo in v3 to Ming Liu in v4, with slight author-block alignment changes and an updated arXiv version/date stamp. Body wording and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Raster images are downsampled and recompressed throughout the figures; for example, Figure S3’s embedded images change from 512×512 to 200×200 pixels. Figure and table content, captions, structure and placement are retained.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, explanations and limitations are unchanged. v4 updates correspondence metadata and reduces the PDF from about 51 MB to 12 MB, trading fine image detail at high zoom for a smaller file while keeping figures usable. These changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
